name: Justin Aromin
body:
I still don’t know if I am able to fully articulate Paul’s impact on this Earth yet.  I have tried several times to write this and think of every memory I have of him.  I have known Paul since I was 14 and over the past 10+ years as a part of my family so that’s a lot of moments in time.  Every time I think of a moment, I think about what would Paul want Oli to know about him.  What single story could I recount to fully illuminate the character that Paul was and still is presently to so many people!?!  I am not sure I am capable of honoring his legacy in one single memory but a collection of random musings he embodied.  

“Hey man…” was always his greeting to me.  

“Paul Time” was the coined phrase for Paul’s arrival to any family event…always late but sure to be present for the pinnacle moment….always leaving early to get to somewhere else.

“Watermelon Crusher”…Paul claimed his thighs were so strong that he could crush a watermelon with them.  Everyone present for this claim laughed and laughed so much.  We never got to test this one out but I am sure it would have been awesome to watch the attempt.  It still makes me smile to think of this ridiculous boast.

“The Mayor”...Paul was a people person in every sense.  He could conversate with anyone about anything.  He had a free spirit and an ability to connect.  I think he even said things (not even sure he believed them) to get a conversation or debate going.  I think my sister could attest to this.  One New Year’s Eve, after we left a bar off Thayer St., we were walking to our car when we passed a house that was having a party.  Paul walked by and noticed the door was open and just welcomed himself in.  I went home, Paul stayed.

“DJ Pauly Danger” was his professional alias.  Music was what originally bonded Paul and I in high school.  Paul knew I loved going to shows in Providence.  Whenever he could, he would have his dad contact his old friend, Rich Lupo, and get us tickets or even on the guestlist to a show.  We saw a lot of shows together and as we got older, we both separately fell in love with reggae music.  My fascination and obsession was anything Marley or Wailers related and his was more modern and dancehall.  He would give me grief about Marley stuff being so commercialized but he would always dedicate one Marley related song whenever I came out to see him DJ.  I vividly remember Paul dedicating and playing “Who the Cap Fit” for me when he opened for Bob’s grandson, Jo Mersa Marley at Ocean Mist many moons ago.

“Uncle Pauly” was what we called Paul in our house.  He sincerely enjoyed my kids and introduced them to all the things you forget about as an adult.  July 4 will never be the same again without Uncle Pauly bringing some fireworks for the kids.  Truly bringing the danger to my house and neighborhood. My son Jack loved going over to Uncle Paul’s to work in the yard with him.  He taught my daughter Eleanor how to swing her legs to go higher on the swing set.  Every family outing, he made every effort to engage and entertain them. In retrospect, he was an amazing Uncle to Jack and Eleanor.

“Paul with the Dad Face”...This is how I will always remember him.  The last time he came to my house was with Oli while my sister was at work.  They came by to cool off during the hot summer weather.  Paul was in full dad-mode with every item a 1 year old would need.  Oli got wet playing in the sprinklers with Eleanor and Paul needed to change him to dry him off.  Oli started to run around with no diaper, and then proceeded to urinate on the ground…it was a sight to witness because Oli seemed genuinely proud of this new talent.  Paul’s face was a look of pride and joy, not disgust or disappointment, in this moment.  Paul had the prideful dad-look you can only achieve when you love your kid more than anything in this world.  I even remarked to him, “...these are those dad moments.”  I know Paul loved being a dad more than anything else in this world.

I sincerely miss the guy and promise to share with Oli all of these moments and more.  

Cheers Paul!
